This is because in SDK-style projects, the SDK imports happen both before and after the project file content. The `CompileDependsOn` property is defined in the SDK .targets files which are imported AFTER the project body.

In SDK-style projects, property assignments in the project body happen BEFORE the SDK .targets are imported. So when we set `<CompileDependsOn>$(CompileDependsOn);GenerateApiClient</CompileDependsOn>`, at that point `$(CompileDependsOn)` is empty (not yet defined by the SDK). Then the SDK .targets define their own `CompileDependsOn` without including our value.
 
The solution is to either use `BeforeTargets="CoreCompile"` to hook into the target dependency system directly, or place the property assignment in a `.targets` file that gets imported after the SDK. Since `CompileDependsOn` is defined in the SDK's .targets files that load after the project body, setting it in the project file won't persist through the SDK's later definitions. So the real issue is that setting `CompileDependsOn` directly replaces the entire chain instead of extending it, which loses the SDK's compilation targets. The fix is to append to the existing value using `$(CompileDependsOn);GenerateApiClient`, but in SDK-style projects this needs to happen after the SDK imports its targets, which typically requires a separate `.targets` file or using `BeforeTargets="CoreCompile"` with proper incrementality markers. is to append to the chain using `<CompileDependsOn>$(CompileDependsOn);GenerateApiClient</CompileDependsOn>` so the SDK's existing targets remain intact.
